title: Packet-prefetch + deferred toollets: streaming handoff PRD sketch
content:
Context and intent:

This is a working PRD sketch exploring a compact protocol and SDK patterns for two related problems we keep hitting in hosted streaming: 1) reducing latency and token costs for common short-turn tool-invocation patterns (search, DB-lookup, small code exec) via predictive prefetching (we call the primitive a packet-prefetch) and 2) enabling safe deferred execution of 'toollets' (small discrete tool calls that can be resolved off the main response path and stitched back into the stream when available). The goal is better tail-latency behavior for hosted streaming SDKs while keeping developer ergonomics simple and observability intact.

Why this matters now:
- Customers increasingly use tool-calls inside streamed sessions (e.g., search, vector DB, lambda run) and expect near-interactive latencies.
- Naive blocking tool-call patterns blow up P50 and P95 for short responses and drive up token counts as clients re-ask or wait for full answers.
- We already have batching, KV caching, and model fallbacks; packet-prefetch + deferred toollets are complementary levers that reduce synchronous waits and make degradation graceful.

High-level approach:
1) Packet-prefetch: server-side hinting and client-choice prefetch queues that surface expected external operations the model will request. Hints are lightweight payloads returned as an early frame in the stream with probabilities and time-budget guidance. SDKs can optionally pre-exec these with configurable SLAs.
2) Deferred toollets: opaque, idempotent tool call units that may be executed out-of-band and merged into the stream as 'patch frames' or summarized placeholders. Toollets are first-class in the handshake and have execution metadata (expected latency, fallback policy, schema for insertion).

User / developer stories (non-exhaustive):
- As a product engineer embedding a chat assistant, I want the assistant to show fast skeleton responses while search results arrive in the next 50–200ms patch, avoiding a full refresh.
- As an infra owner, I want predictable tail-latency budgets by allowing low-cost prefetching of highly-likely toollets and controlled abort/hedge behavior to limit wasted work.
- As an observability owner, I want explicit telemetry for predicted vs. executed toollets and one-line traceability from initial hint to final merged frame.

API surface sketches (stream frames):
- initial frame: { type: "partial", text: "...", tool_hints: [{id, op, confidence, ttl_ms, schema}], session_token }
- tool request frame (from model): { type: "tool_request", id, op, args_schema }
- tool patch frame (from server/tool executed): { type: "tool_patch", id, op, status, payload, merge_hint }
- final commit frame: { type: "commit", seq, trace_id }

Notes: these are conceptual; wire format will be compact JSON lines but follow our existing incremental schema patterns (frame ids, idempotency tokens). Frames must be small and amenable to streaming partials.

SDK ergonomics (opinionated defaults):
- Opt-in prefetch: default OFF. Higher tiers/hosted clients can enable 'aggressive' prefetch for reduced latency at cost.
- Prefetch policy object: {parallelism: 2, max inflight ms: 400, cost_threshold: "cheap-only"} — simple knobs to control waste.
- Toollet interface in SDK: fast call method that returns a Future/Promise for patch insertion and exposes cancel/abort semantics. Example: client.toollet.execute(prefetchToken).then(insertPatch).catch(insertPlaceholder).
- Merge behavior: SDK provides merge hooks and a small default merging algorithm (text splice with pointer anchors + structured payload insertion for typed schemas). Developers can override with merge callbacks.

Observability and telemetry requirements:
- Telemetry events: hint_emitted, hint_prefetch_started, hint_prefetch_completed, toollet_executed, toollet_failed, tool_patch_merged, patch_skipped, patch_hedged.
- Each event must include trace_id, session_id, frame_id, hint_confidence, execution_latency_ms, and resource_cost_estimate.
- Aggregates: prefetch hit rate, wasted-prefetch-cost, median patch insertion latency, P95 patch merge latency, and patch-schema-mismatch rate.

Fallback and safety model:
- If a prefetched toollet fails/aborts, the SDK inserts a small graceful placeholder frame ("source unavailable") and optionally triggers a model re-prompt (costly).
- Server can mark toollets 'best-effort' or 'blocking'. Blocking toollets block final commit frames and are not prefetched without explicit developer opt-in.
- Idempotency: every toollet has idempotency key derived from session + op + args-hash. Servers must support duplicate execution suppression.

Schema and structured output considerations:
- Toollet payloads must declare a small schema (json-schema-lite) to allow safe insertion and validation at merge time.
- For typed outputs (tables, JSON objects), the SDK should prefer patch frames that carry both human text and typed payloads so clients can show partial structured UI before full consistency.
- Versioning: toollet schemas carry a schema_version and a compatibility flag (breaking | additive) so the client can choose to reject or attempt best-effort merge when versions mismatch.

Operational and cost model:
- Prefetch work is charged to the customer that enabled prefetch. We need quota mechanisms and a separate cost meter for prefetch attempts vs. successful merges.
- Autoscaling signals: prefetch burst patterns must be smoothed; expose prefetch_rate metrics to dimension capacity planning.

Experimentation matrix (MVP -> Beta -> GA):
- MVP (rolling alpha): basic frame types, server-side hint emission, very conservative SDK prefetch (parallelism 1, short ttl 150ms), telemetry + logs. Restrict to internal beta customers.
- Beta: support structured payloads with lite-schema, idempotency, hedging rules, UI merge hook defaults, opt-in workspace toggle. Pilot with 2 customers.
- GA: full policy panel in Console, billing split, SLA guidance, SDK maturity (JS, Python, Go), and documented fallback patterns.

Risks and unresolved questions (open):
- Prediction accuracy: how often will prefetch hints be wrong and what is the acceptable wasted compute? Need data.
- Privacy/compliance: prefetching calls to customer tools might carry PII and execute unintended side effects. Must add explicit developer gating and opt-in controls.
- UX complexity: merging partial structured outputs into apps is app-specific; we should provide clear best-effort defaults but not overpromise.
- Cross-region: prefetched toollets executed in a different region than the streaming client could violate data residency rules. Need region-aware policy.

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Serving-runtime: add a lightweight hint emitter step in incremental generator that runs after early tokens (first 12 tokens heuristic) and emits top-K probable tool ops with confidence scores.
- Router/runtime: attach prefetch tokens to downstream worker to optionally trigger an execution microtask in a prefetch pool. Prefetch pool uses small instances for cheap ops and enforces short time budget.
- SDKs: new Toollet API primitives, default merge plugin, and telemetry integration. Keep initial API surface minimal (one or two calls).

Milestones and next steps (30/60/90):
- 30d: prototype hint emitter + frame serialization; basic JS SDK prefetch that logs events (no billing).
- 60d: internal beta toy demo with two sample tool adapters (search, snippet-runner), gather metrics on hit-rate & wasted cost.
- 90d: design Console toggles, quota billing draft, and formalize telemetry schema.

Appendix — quick examples (developer-facing):
1) Stream snippet showing hint then patch:
- Frame 1 (partial): "We should check the last PR for code references...", tool_hints: [{id: "h1", op: "code_search", confidence: 0.87, ttl_ms: 300}]
- SDK prefetch executes code_search(h1) -> returns d1
- Frame 2 (tool_patch): {id: "h1", status: "ok", payload: {summary: "found 3 matches", top_hit: {file: "a.py", snippet: "def foo():"}}, merge_hint: "append-summaries"}
- UI merges summary into the partial response in-line.

TODOs (short):
- Run simulation on 10k recorded streaming sessions to estimate hint accuracy and wasted prefetch cost. (owner: Julien)
- Draft Console UI for per-workspace toggle and cost guardrails. (owner: Maya)
- Security review for prefetch gating and KMS/HSM considerations. (owner: Liam)

Notes to reviewers:
This doc intentionally mixes conceptual framing with low-level sketches. Feedback wanted on the risk appetite for prefetch waste, preferred defaults for SDKs, and whether we should treat toollets as first-class in the API or keep them as advisory hints initially.

History: created as a follow-up to multiple field reports of high tail latency in short-turn streaming flows during Q3 2025 customer trials.

End of sketch.
